== Research Notes ==
=== Parish household review, 23 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1616|Andrew Glasgow]] → [[Glasgow-1218|David Glasgow]]: 63% → 95% (confident). The Swinton and Simprin transcript, OPR 755/1 item 8 p.19, records Andrew born 25 November 1767, baptised 29 November, parents David Glasgow and Janet Hood, residence Longbank. Exact child dates and the full parental couple identify the David/Janet adult household already represented by David-1218. This resolves the earlier unquoted-parent-fields limitation; the held regional duplicate review documents no concrete competing David/Janet Hood household. 95% identifies Andrew’s father as the David of the Janet Hood household. It does not establish that adult as the 1744 Stichill child, 1798 Kelso weaver, or later Edinburgh/Ireland man. Those identities and Janet’s childhood require their own evidence. The companion index represents the same baptism, not independent corroboration. Original register image uninspected.

[[Glasgow-1218|David Glasgow]] → [[Glasgow-1238|James Glasgow]]: 97% → 70% (probable). The 1744 Stichill child account names James and Elizabeth, supported by their 1740 marriage and subsequent local children; its recorded-child father clause retains 97% conditional confidence. Identifying this child with the 1767 David/Janet Hood adult is plausible at age about 23 in neighbouring Borders parishes and with a later son James. The held regional comparison records no suitable competing David, but no marriage or residence continuity directly bridges these identities. The complete adult-to-James-1238 placement is assessed 70%. The previous 97% measured the 1744 child’s parentage, not the complete later adult ancestry. Preserve it conditionally; no contradictory parent clause has been found. Andrew’s 95% identifies the 1767 father without establishing his childhood. Kelso militia/weaver, Edinburgh, Ireland and William Glass/Tristan da Cunha identities remain separate. Original register images uninspected.

Earlier dated percentages and interpretations below are retained as superseded history for these pairs; the current assessments and their specific identity limits are stated here. No live WikiTree changes have been made by this local review.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1238]] is assessed at 97% (proved). David’s 1744 Stichill child account names James and Elizabeth. The existing James/Elizabeth Tait marriage of 1740 and subsequent Stichill children identify a specific local parental household rather than just a matching father name.

Record-defined child and Tait household97%; David’s later adult identification and James’s own 1712 ancestry are separate. Original uninspected.

Next useful test: Check the original 1744 entry’s full maternal name and residence.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMMQ-472 https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FMMQ-472]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.


=== Possible James Glasgow and father David, Kelso militia list, 1798 ===
James Glasgow, son to David Glasgow, is named in the Kelso parish militia ballot list accompanying a Jedburgh notice dated 29 September 1798.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395735887/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1798-10-04, p.1].</ref>

The entry expressly identifies the listed James as David’s son; it does not say "junior". David is described with a weaving descriptor whose exact reading remains qualified. Selection in a militia ballot does not prove completed service or identify James’s mother.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1218]]. For the named father David, Uncertain birth before 13 April 1744 at Stitchel and regional context are compatible with the father David. This is an upper birth bound, not an exact year; the existing link to James-1222 is derived from the family tree and no occupation connection is checked.
